# MDL602 · `mysql-include-directive`

<!-- Generated by tools/gendocs from internal/rules: do not edit. -->

`!include` or `!includedir`: a MySQL directive that mydumper does not follow.

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | connection |
| Default severity | warning |
| Fix | — |
| Design references | C3, F6 |
| Proven on real mydumper by | [`mdl602-include-directive-in-tool-group`](../../e2e/scenarios/mdl602-include-directive-in-tool-group.txtar), [`mdl602-include-directive-in-client-group`](../../e2e/scenarios/mdl602-include-directive-in-client-group.txtar) |

## Why

MySQL option files accept `!include FILE` and `!includedir DIR`. mydumper reads its configuration with GLib, which knows no such directive: the line is a key named `!include FILE`. Only the MySQL client library, which re-reads the file for the connection, follows it.

In [mydumper] or [myloader] the key is passed to GLib's option parser as an unknown option: mydumper aborts at startup up to v1.0.0-1 and ignores it afterwards (error). Elsewhere, such as [client], the connection settings of the included file work, but any [mydumper] section or table section in it is ignored (warning).

## Example

With mydumper v0.19.3-3:

❌ Before:

```ini
[client]
!include /etc/mysql/backup.cnf
[mydumper]
threads=2
```

```text
2:1-2:31 warning MDL602[mysql-include-directive] `!include` is a MySQL directive: mydumper reads it as a key and never opens the included file; only the MySQL client library does
  = The connection settings of the included file apply, but any [mydumper], [myloader] or table section in it is ignored.
```

## Configuration

Enabled by default. To change its severity or turn it off:

```yaml
rules:
  severity:
    MDL602: warning   # or error, info, off
```

To accept one occurrence, put `# mydumper-lint: disable-next-line=MDL602` on the line above it.
